injuryReports.name: Alec Anderson
injuryReports.returnComment: Anderson didn't practice Thursday or Friday due to an ankle injury, but he was able to log a limited session Saturday to have at least a chance of suiting up Monday. If Anderson ends up being sidelined, Austin Corbett could draw the start at left guard.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Spencer Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown missed last Sunday's win over Baltimore, but he'll be back in action Monday after logging an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week. His return will be especially critical if fellow starting offensive tackle Dion Dawkins (ribs, questionable) isn't able to suit up.
injuryReports.injury: Brown (back) does not have a designation for Monday's matchup in Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Dion Dawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Dawkins didn't practice at all this week due to an injury to his ribs, but he still has a chance to suit up. Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, the veteran tackle was hurt in the first half of last Sunday's win over Baltimore but was able to finish out the contest. Dawkins said he'll do everything he can to be ready for Monday Night Football, so he may be a true game-time decision.
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: Tyrell Shavers
injuryReports.returnComment: Shavers remains on the reserve/PUP list with a knee injury despite logging three consecutive full practices during Week 9 prep. The wide receiver could return to the active roster ahead of Monday night's showdown with the Vikings, but it will be contingent on the Bills creating a spot on the 53-man roster in time.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL

injuryReports.name: Keon Coleman
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, Coleman again was spotted in a red non-contact jersey Saturday and eventually went down as a limited participant for a third consecutive practice. Despite the restrictions this week, though, Coleman is ready to suit up for an eighth straight game to begin the season, having put up a 20-287-3 line on 27 targets to date.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest in Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: DJ Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: While logging three straight limited practices during Week 9 prep, Moore continued to wear a red non-contact jersey due to the AC joint sprain that he's been dealing with since Week 2. Now that he's in the clear for Monday's matchup, he'll look to build upon the 16-260-2 line on 27 targets that he's racked up through five eppearances on the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Moore (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest at Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Palmer
injuryReports.returnComment: Palmer exited last Sunday's win against the Ravens in the first half and wasn't able to return due to a hamstring injury. After not practicing Thursday or Friday, the Bills opted to keep him on the sidelines in Week 9, meaning Greg Dortch, Skyler Bell and/or Tyrell Shavers (knee, IR) may see WR reps behind the team's top trio at the position.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Ty Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: A quick return after Thursday's absence confirms Johnson isn't dealing with a serious illness. He should be fine for his usual role on passing downs Monday night at Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson (illness) was a full practice participant Friday.

injuryReports.name: Dalton Kincaid
injuryReports.returnComment: Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo previously noted that Kincaid had shed his red non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, and the tight end's full participation in the session paves the way for him to be in uniform Monday night against the Vikings. Over his last two games, Kincaid (who overall is tied for first among Bills in catches (27) and leads the team in receiving yards (401)) has logged an 11-124-1 receiving line, a pace that keeps him relevant from a fantasy perspective.
injuryReports.injury: Kincaid (chest) was a full participant in Friday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Dee Alford
injuryReports.returnComment: Alford was inactive for Sunday's win over the Ravens, though it appears he will be back on the field when the Bills face the Vikings on Monday night. With the 28-year-old back in the equation, Te'Cory Couch and Maxwell Hairston will likely see fewer snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Alford (ankle) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Hancock
injuryReports.returnComment: Hancock has been on IR since late September while recovering from a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2 versus Detroit. The cornerback had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, and if he isn't activated in that time frame, he will remain on IR for the rest of the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Greg Gaines
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Dawson Knox
injuryReports.returnComment: It's a typical receiving line for Knox, whose main contributions come in the blocking department. Knox has nine grabs for 42 yards and one touchdown across seven appearances this season. He'd likely need multiple wideout and tight-end injuries to be a fantasy consideration.
injuryReports.injury: Knox caught one of two targets for six yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Ray Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Bills throttling the Ravens and James Cook suffering a neck injury late in the game, Davis got some added run in the fourth quarter. If Cook misses any time, Davis would be the likely early-down replacement, with Ty Johnson sticking to his role on passing downs and four- and two-minute situations.
injuryReports.injury: Davis rushed six times for 30 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Bass
injuryReports.returnComment: Bass converted multiple long-range field goals for the Bills after the offense stalled several times due to drops. The kicker succeeded from 56 yards, 22 yards and 51 yards in the contest. Bass has converted all 16 of his field-goal attempts and is 21-for-23 on PATs through seven games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Bass made all three of his field-goal attempts as well as three PATs in the Bills' 36-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Greg Dortch
injuryReports.returnComment: Dortch has been serving as Buffalo's top return man throughout the season, but he continues to see limited involvement as a receiver. The 28-year-old hasn't played more than five offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances and has yet to draw a target.
injuryReports.injury: Dortch went without a target while logging four of the Bills' 82 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He returned one kickoff for 22 yards and three punts for 40 yards.

injuryReports.name: Khalil Shakir
injuryReports.returnComment: Shakir initially appeared to get in the end zone for a six-yard touchdown early in the first quarter, but he was ruled out at the one-yard line after review. Josh Allen then punched in the one-yard touchdown two plays later. On the day, Shakir paced the Bills with his five grabs and tied for second on the team in targets, one behind DJ Moore. Shakir has yet to hit 100 yards in a game this season and has just one touchdown, settling in as a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy, especially when both Moore and Dalton Kincaid are healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Shakir caught five of six targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: James Cook III
injuryReports.returnComment: Cook gave the Bills some breathing room with a five-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to extend Buffalo's lead to 23-10. He was evaluated for a head injury later in the game but received clearance to return and notched one more carry after that point. After being held to 57 rushing yards without a touchdown by the Texans in Week 1, Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in six consecutive games. Extending that streak won't be easy in Week 9 against Minnesota's elite defense on MNF.
injuryReports.injury: Cook rushed 21 times for 80 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Josh Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen capped the opening drive with a one-yard touchdown plunge on which he went airborne to stretch the ball over the goal line. He struggled as a passer in the first half, including a first-quarter interception, but Allen heated up after halftime to post his highest passing yards total since a 334-yard Week 1 performance. Allen's 11-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore (knee) in the fourth quarter gave Allen sole possession of first place in Bills history with 259 passing touchdowns, including postseason play. He added a 23-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Kincaid on the next drive as the Bills pulled away from a Ravens team that lost top two QBs Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe). Allen has led the Bills to a 6-1 record heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the 6-1 Vikings.
injuryReports.injury: Allen completed 21 of 34 passes for 289 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He added 30 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown on seven rushing attempts.

injuryReports.name: Tyrique Stevenson Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: A thumb injury left Stevenson uncertain for Week 9, and his availability will not officially be revealed until 90 minutes before Sunday's 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. However -- per the report -- with help from a splint, it appears he will be ready to take the field.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Malik Muhammad II
injuryReports.returnComment: Muhammad missed last week's victory over the Seahawks due to a toe injury sustained in Week 7, but it appears he will miss only the lone contest.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Kyle Monangai
injuryReports.returnComment: Monangai was able to get back on the practice field Friday for the first time since suffering a turf-toe injury versus the Jets on Oct. 4, but his limited showing in that session seemingly won't be enough to clear him to suit up Sunday. The Bears have a Week 10 bye on tap, so it comes as no surprise that the team likely will hold off on Monangai's return for two more weeks. Yet again, D'Andre Swift will pace Chicago's backfield this weekend, with Roschon Johnson also on hand for RB reps.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Salvon Ahmed
injuryReports.returnComment: Ahmed is set to be elevated for the first time since signing with Chicago's practice squad in September. With Zavier Scott (wrist) being placed on injured reserve Thursday and Kyle Monangai dealing with thumb and toe injuries, Ahmed could be called upon to provide additional depth behind D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson against Tampa Bay.
injuryReports.injury: The Bears elevated Ahmed from their practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Grady Jarrett
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing the Bears' walk-through practice Wednesday, Jarrett logged a limited practice Thursday and then upgraded again to a full practice Friday. He should start on the interior of the defensive line next to Jeffery Simmons again in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Jarrett (groin) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Zavier Scott
injuryReports.returnComment: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Wrist

injuryReports.name: Kentavius Street
injuryReports.returnComment: Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Braxton Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones underwent right knee surgery Tuesday, and as a result, he will be forced to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign. In his absence, Theo Benedet (shoulder) will continue to operate as the team's primary option at left tackle.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Stephen Carlson
injuryReports.returnComment: When Cole Kmet went to the Bears' injured reserve list with a season-ending knee injury following Week 7, it left the team with just two healthy tight ends on its active roster, so the move gives the club some much-needed depth at the position. As long as starter Colston Loveland and rookie third-rounder Sam Roush remain available, though, Carlson's role will likely be limited as the season progresses.
injuryReports.injury: Chicago signed Carlson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster Wednesday, Brendan Sugrue of USA Today reports.

injuryReports.name: Sam Roush
injuryReports.returnComment: With Cole Kmet landing on injured reserve with a season-ending knee injury, Roush stepped into an increased role on offense, as his 53 percent snap share represented a season-best mark. However, the added playing time didn't translate to any involvement in the passing game, as Roush ran just 12 routes on the night. The Bears' frequent usage of two-tight-end formations should continue to prop up Roush's snap counts, but he's likely to be utilized mainly as a blocker when he's on the field.
injuryReports.injury: Roush went without a target while playing 37 of the Bears' 70 snaps on offense in Monday's 34-17 win over the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Roschon Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: With Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) inactive for a fourth straight game, Johnson continued to serve as the No. 2 running back behind D'Andre Swift. Unsurprisingly, Swift (27 carries for 69 yards and three touchdowns) handled the brunt of the work out of the backfield, with Johnson taking the field for just 14 of the team's 70 offensive snaps. If Monangai is able to make it back for Sunday's matchup with the Buccaneers, Johnson's playing time on offense could disappear entirely.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson carried five times for 17 yards and added an 11-yard reception on his lone target in Monday's 34-17 win over the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Jayden Loving
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Cairo Santos
injuryReports.returnComment: Santos made 44- and 38-yard field goals in the second quarter. It was a nice bounce-back game for the veteran kicker after he'd missed a field-goal try in each of the previous three games. For the season, Santos is 13-for-17 on FGAs and a perfect 25-for-25 on PATs. Being attached to the Bears offense makes Santos an attractive fantasy kicker.
injuryReports.injury: Santos made both field-goal tries and all four PATs in Monday night's 34-17 win over the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Caleb Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams helped set the tone for the Bears' statement road victory by leading a 17-play, 80-yard march that absorbed 8:32 of the first quarter, one that the third-year signal-caller capped off with a one-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden. Williams then managed the game effectively from that point forward, avoiding mistakes while leaning on a workhorse performance from D'Andre Swift (27 carries, three touchdowns) and an often dominating effort from his defense. Williams now has a three-game streak of interception-free performances and is up to 1,267 passing yards through five contests heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Williams completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions and rushed twice for one yard in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Kalif Raymond
injuryReports.returnComment: Raymond's most memorable contribution was a 39-yard dash on a third-down play early in the fourth quarter to take the ball down to Seattle's five-yard line and set up a D'Andre Swift touchdown. Though he didn't put up massive numbers, Raymond's 53 total yards were his most since Week 3 and represented more yardage than he had recorded over his previous four games combined. Raymond remains a shaky fantasy play given his recent numbers, and a Week 9 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that has been pretty stingy on wideouts doesn't improve his outlook.
injuryReports.injury: Raymond finished Monday's 34-17 win against Seattle with two catches for 14 yards on three targets along with one rush for 39 yards.

injuryReports.name: Rome Odunze
injuryReports.returnComment: Odunze led the Bears in receiving yards on the night while finishing second in receptions and targets. The third-year wideout's catch and yardage totals both qualified as his second highest of the season, and Odunze now has 156 receiving yards over the last pair of contests for his most productive two-game stretch this season. Odunze is averaging a career-best 16.7 yards per catch and already has a career-high 14 receptions of 20-plus yards heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Odunze brought in four of six targets for 87 yards in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Luther Burden III
injuryReports.returnComment: Burden tied Colston Loveland for the team lead in both receptions and targets, and he was on the receiving end of Caleb Williams' one touchdown pass of the night. The second-year wideout's scoring grab came from one yard out in the first quarter and was his third of the season, and Burden now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets over the last three games heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Burden secured seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Colston Loveland
injuryReports.returnComment: Loveland continued his upward trajectory by tying Luther Burden for the team lead in catches and targets, and he finished second in receiving yards to Rome Odunze. The second-year tight end's fourth-quarter fumble was costly for the moment, however, as Loveland lost the ball at the Bears' 21-yard line following an eight-yard reception, and the turnover ultimately led to the Seahawks' final touchdown of the contest. Nevertheless, Loveland now has at least six receptions in four of the last five games, including three straight, and he's drawn 21 targets over the last pair of contests alone heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Loveland secured seven of nine targets for 65 yards and lost a fumble in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: D'Andre Swift
injuryReports.returnComment: Swift put in a full night's work while repeatedly butting heads with the Seahawks' elite run defense, as his longest run went for only seven yards, and he averaged 2.6 yards per carry overall. He sealed the win for Chicago with his third touchdown of the game, a five-yard run with 4:41 remaining. That score was preceded by one- and five-yard TDs earlier in the second half, and Swift's carry total was a season high. The veteran running back is up to a career-high 10 rushing touchdowns heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Swift rushed 27 times for 69 yards and three touchdowns and brought in two of three targets for 10 yards in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Case Keenum
injuryReports.returnComment: Keenum will serve as the No. 3 QB for the third straight week, while Tyson Bagent slots in as the primary backup behind starter Caleb Williams. Keenum will only be eligible to enter the contest if both Williams and Bagent are forced out of the game.
injuryReports.injury: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but will operate as the Bears' emergency third quarterback for Monday night's matchup against the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Jack Sanborn
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanborn was unable to play against the Patriots in Week 7 due to a concussion, but he was a full participant in all three practices of Week 8 prep, and he has cleared the league's protocol after passing an evaluation from an independent neurologist. He has four tackles (three solo) across six regular-season games while serving mostly on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Sanborn (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Odell Beckham Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Beckham kicked off the season with the Giants but was targeted just one time through the first three contests before the team released him Sept. 29. He then joined the Vikings on the practice squad and was elevated for Week 5 but eventually was inactive. Thus, if Beckham is able to avoid such a listing Monday against the Bills, it'll mark the sixth different organization in which he's suited up in his career.
injuryReports.injury: The Vikings are signing Beckham from the practice squad to the active roster, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Van Ginkel
injuryReports.returnComment: Van Ginkel was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Saturday. He's thus clear to suit up on Monday Night Football against the Bills. That's a big deal for the Vikings in their quest to slow down Josh Allen, as Van Ginkel leads the team with 6.5 sacks through seven games.
injuryReports.injury: Van Ginkel (chest) doesn't have a designation for Monday's matchup against the Bills, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Demond Claiborne
injuryReports.returnComment: Claiborne didn't practice Friday or Saturday after suffering a knee injury in practice Wednesday. Head coach Kevin O'Connell said he doesn't think Claiborne will need surgery but added that the team is still evaluating the injury. The running back has played sparingly this season, logging 18 offensive snaps through four games and tallying 13 yards on six carries along with eight yards on two receptions.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jauan Jennings
injuryReports.returnComment: Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Jennings suffered a calf injury at Thursday's practice that is serious enough to sideline him for at least one game. Jennings' next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 15 in Green Bay, while Tai Felton and Myles Price are in for some offensive snaps this week behind the top WR duo of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Kyler Murray
injuryReports.returnComment: Murray emerged from last Sunday's loss to the Lions with a sore hamstring, and O'Connell told Alec Lewis of The Athletic on Thursday that the quarterback was unlikely to play in Week 9 but also wasn't an IR consideration. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Saturday morning that Murray is in recovery mode from a Grade 2 hamstring strain that will sideline him Monday and potentially beyond that point. Now that Murray officially is out for his second contest of the campaign, Carson Wentz is set to see his first game action since Week 2.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Christian Darrisaw
injuryReports.returnComment: Darrisaw began Week 9 prep with a limited session Thursday, but he was able to log a full session Friday. As such, he should be good to go for Monday's matchup against Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Darrisaw (shoulder) was a full practice participant Friday.

injuryReports.name: Jay Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Max Brosmer
injuryReports.returnComment: It would likely take an injury to Wentz for Brosmer to get into the game, but the latter moves one step closer to getting on the field for the first time in 2026. Brosmer didn't look like an NFL-caliber QB as a rookie in 2025, posting a 0:4 TD:INT across seven appearances, including two starts.
injuryReports.injury: Brosmer is set to back up Carson Wentz against the Bills on Monday, as Kyler Murray (hamstring) won't play, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Carson Wentz
injuryReports.returnComment: Wentz will get the Week 9 assignment at QB for the Vikings, with Kyler Murray viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Max Brosmer will be the team's backup versus Buffalo, and perhaps longer than that should Murray's injury linger. Wentz thus represents an option for those in Superflex formats or otherwise are in need of signal-caller help due to injury or bye week issues.
injuryReports.injury: Wentz is stated to start Monday night's game against the Bills, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: DeeJay Dallas
injuryReports.returnComment: Dallas will return to the active roster after playing in the first five contests of the year with the Vikings before being released and ultimately returning to the team as a member of the practice squad in late October. The running back has rushed four times for 14 yards and caught all four of his targets for 34 yards over seven contests with Minnesota this year, and he figures to operate in an extreme depth role behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason on Monday night versus Buffalo.
injuryReports.injury: Dallas was signed to the Vikings' active roster Wednesday, Craig Peters of the team's official website reports.

injuryReports.name: Eric Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson finished second on the Vikings in stops, behind only Josh Metellus (13). One of his tackles was a sack of Jared Goff for a 10-yard loss on Detroit's first drive of the game, resulting in a Detroit punt. Wilson has 3.0 sacks through seven games, so he could surpass the career-best mark of 6.5 sacks he recorded over 17 regular-season games last year.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson registered 11 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, in Sunday's loss to Detroit.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Metellus
injuryReports.returnComment: Metellus led Minnesota in tackles and recorded a season-high mark in the process. He's been a consistent presence for the Vikings' tough defense this season, playing every defensive snap in six of the team's seven contests so far. Metellus is up to 50 stops through seven games, putting him on pace for the third triple-digit tackle campaign of his career.
injuryReports.injury: Metellus recorded 13 tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass in a Week 8 defeat against Detroit.

injuryReports.name: Byron Murphy Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Murphy tied for third on Minnesota in tackles on a day when four Vikings finished with double-digit stops. The tackle tally was Murphy's highest of the season and snapped a four-game stretch of posting three stops or fewer. The veteran cornerback is enjoying a nice campaign overall, as he's tallied three interceptions so far, tying for second in the NFL in that category.
injuryReports.injury: Murphy registered 10 tackles (eight solo) in a loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Blake Cashman
injuryReports.returnComment: Cashman was one of four Vikings to notch double-digit stops in the team's first loss of the season. The veteran linebacker has recorded at least seven stops in each of his seven games this season and has registered double-digit tackles three times. He's well beyond pace for a fourth consecutive season of triple-digit tackles, as he already has 64 stops (including 4.5 sacks) through seven contests.
injuryReports.injury: Cashman finished Sunday's loss to Detroit with 10 tackles (five solo).

injuryReports.name: Will Reichard
injuryReports.returnComment: Reichard missed a 57-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker's miss proved costly as the Vikings lost a four-point game that went down to the wire. Reichard is now 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts and 10-for-10 on PATs through seven regular-season games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Reichard missed his sole field-goal attempt and made his sole PAT in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: T.J. Hockenson
injuryReports.returnComment: Hockenson secured an eight-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter to give the Vikings a 15-12 lead, and he's now up to 31 grabs for 295 yards and three touchdowns on 37 targets through seven games this season. Hockenson, though, missed all but two offensive snaps in the Week 5 win over the Saints after suffering a concussion. A favorite target for Kyler Murray in the middle and short areas of the field, Hockenson has settled in as a lower-end TE1 in fantasy. He gets a plus matchup with the Bills next Monday night in another spot the Minnesota offense may be forced to push the gas pedal.
injuryReports.injury: Hockenson caught four of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Addison
injuryReports.returnComment: Addison's big play was a 51-yard catch over the top of the defense in the fourth quarter to set the offense up at the 10-yard line. T.J. Hockenson scored a go-ahead touchdown two plays later. Addison's eight targets on the day were one fewer than Justin Jefferson, but it was the former who paced the team in receiving yards. Playing in a Minnesota offense that doesn't push the ball down the field much or focus on its outside receivers, Addison has just 16 catches for 249 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets through six games this season. He'll be a fantasy WR4 with upside next Monday night against a leaky Bills secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Addison caught three of eight targets for 66 yards in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones shook off the knee injury that had knocked him out of a Week 7 win over the Colts to head into Sunday without a designation. However, the veteran finished with a season low in carries and rushing yards. Jones has just 13 combined rush attempts -- a number partly influenced by the aforementioned early exit against Indianapolis -- in the two games since Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve, and it remains to be seen if the modest role will persist in a Week 9 home matchup against the Bills on Monday night, Nov. 9.
injuryReports.injury: Jones rushed five times for 22 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Mason
injuryReports.returnComment: Playing in his second game since returning from an IR stint due to a thumb injury, Mason paced the Vikings' ground attack in carries but finished two yards behind Aaron Jones, who logged five totes. Mason also wasn't targeted for the second time in three games, and Minnesota's running game figures to continue in a fantasy-averse timeshare between the two. Mason will look to make inroads against what has been an improved Bills run defense in a Week 9 home showdown on Monday night, Nov. 9.
injuryReports.injury: Mason rushed eight times for 20 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Emeka Egbuka
injuryReports.returnComment: On the heels of two games on the sideline due to a concussion and a foot injury, Egbuka kicked off this week as a non-participant Wednesday before logging back-to-back full sessions Thursday and Friday. Despite clearing the protocol for head injuries ahead of Week 8 action, he was listed as questionable with the foot issue ahead of Sunday's matchup, but Pelissero's report indicates Egbuka is trending toward active status. Egbuka's availability will be clarified approximately 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Tristan Wirfs
injuryReports.returnComment: Wirfs appeared on Thursday's injury report as a non-participant with a toe injury. The star left tackle managed to upgrade to limited for Friday's session. The upgrade to limited participation was enough to clear Wirfs of any injury designation, and the veteran protector is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Wirfs (toe) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Tykee Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith was limited at practice by an ankle issue Wednesday and Thursday, but he managed to practice in full Friday and will avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend. He projects to start at safety next to Antoine Winfield in Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (ankle) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Josiah Trotter
injuryReports.returnComment: Trotter was limited by an illness at practice ahead of Week 8, and he ultimately secured a season-low six stops in the win. The rookie linebacker has put together quite the impressive start to his first NFL campaign, compiling 68 total tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pick-six over seven contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Trotter recorded six total tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 16-0 victory over Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Parrish
injuryReports.returnComment: Parrish was able to notch multiple passes defensed for the fifth straight game, and he was able to reel in his second interception of the year, jumping in front of a short pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix in the second quarter. The cornerback has now compiled 36 total tackles (30 solo) and 13 passes defensed, including two interceptions, over seven contests so far during the 2026 regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Parrish registered seven total tackles (four solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 16-0 win over Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Alex Anzalone
injuryReports.returnComment: Anzalone was able to secure exactly six takedowns for the second straight week, but his biggest impact came in the passing game. The linebacker intercepted Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix twice in the first quarter, jumping in front of short passes intended for Drake London and Jahan Dotson. Anzalone has now registered 42 total tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also notching a career-high three interceptions over eight games so far during the 2026 regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Anzalone recorded six total tackles (three solo) and two interceptions in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Kenny Gainwell
injuryReports.returnComment: Gainwell also tended to a hip injury last week, when he got back to full by Friday, but he still entered the weekend listed as questionable for Week 8 action. He proceeded to suit up this past Sunday against the Falcons and split Tampa Bay's backfield with Bucky Irving, logging a 50 percent snap share and going for 140 yards on 25 carries in rainy conditions. Considering Gainwell followed up Wednesday's limited session with an uncapped one Thursday, he's good to go for Sunday's road showdown with the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Gainwell (hip) was a full practice participant Thursday, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jalen McMillan
injuryReports.returnComment: McMillan was initially given a return timetable of 6-to-8 weeks after aggravating a PCL sprain in his left knee in Week 3. Head coach Todd Bowles said McMillan won't have his window to return from IR opened before the Buccaneers face the Bears on Sunday, and Tampa Bay will be on bye the following week, so McMillan's next chance to play won't come until Nov. 22 at Detroit.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - PCL

injuryReports.name: Bauer Sharp
injuryReports.returnComment: After logging single-digit snaps on offense in each of the first six games of the season, Sharp appears to have firmly supplanted Ko Kieft as the Buccaneers' No. 3 tight end behind Cade Otton and Payne Durham. Sharp played a quarter of the snaps in a Week 7 win over the Buccaneers before bumping up to a season-high 32 percent share during Sunday's victory. The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU will likely continue to be utilized mainly as a blocker; he's drawn just one target (a 21-yard reception) while running only nine total routes so far this season.
injuryReports.injury: Sharp went without a target while playing 19 of the Buccaneers' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Tez Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson and the rest of the Buccaneers' pass catchers went without receptions in Week 8 as quarterback Baker Mayfield failed to complete a pass on three attempts in the team's rain-soaked victory. The wide receiver may have another chance to operate in a prominent role on offense if fellow wideout Emeka Egbuka (foot) remains unavailable Sunday versus the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson did not garner a target during Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Ted Hurst III
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with Emeka Egbuka (foot) missing a second straight game, Hurst couldn't catch a break, as the game was played in a downpour. Tampa Bay attempted just three passes during the entire game. Hurst has now gone without a catch in back-to-back games without Egbuka in the lineup. Hurst has minimal fantasy appeal outside of being a hold in dynasty formats.
injuryReports.injury: Hurst failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Sean Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bucs' RB3 played one snap on special teams. He stayed glued to the sideline, as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell ran roughshod all over the Atlanta defense, combining for 52 carries, 310 yards and one touchdown. Tucker won't hold much fantasy value unless one of Irving or Gainwell goes down with an injury.
injuryReports.injury: Tucker didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Cade Otton
injuryReports.returnComment: Playing in rain-soaked conditions, the Bucs attempted just three passes all afternoon, as Baker Mayfield failed to complete any of the three. Otton now has posted back-to-back zero-catch games and has minimal fantasy appeal outside of the deepest of TE-premium formats. He has 19 grabs for 186 yards and no touchdowns on 30 targets through eight games.
injuryReports.injury: Otton wasn't targeted in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Chase McLaughlin
injuryReports.returnComment: The kicker connected from 46, 34 and 42 yards as he accounted for a majority of his team's points. McLaughlin has yet to miss this season, hitting 19 field goals and 17 extra points through eight games.
injuryReports.injury: McLaughlin made all three field-goal attempts and his only extra-point try in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Yaya Diaby
injuryReports.returnComment: Diaby exited this past Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons with the knee injury, which was revealed to be a Grade 2 MCL sprain following an MRI on Monday, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Though Diaby will miss at least one game due to the injury, Bowles expressed hope that the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye would aid the edge rusher's recovery and allow him to avoid a stint on injured reserve.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - MCL

injuryReports.name: Baker Mayfield
injuryReports.returnComment: The afternoon-long rainy conditions in Tampa Bay and the Falcons' defense's complete inability to slow down the Buccaneers' ground attack led to Mayfield barely putting in any work as a passer. In the process, the Bucs became the first team since 1974 to win a game without a single completion, and the bizarre circumstances left Mayfield's fantasy managers with a dead spot in their lineups. Mayfield will naturally be a lot busier when he travels to the Windy City to face the Bears' aggressive defense in a Week 9 road showdown next Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Mayfield failed to complete any of his three pass attempts in the Buccaneers' 16-0 win over the Falcons on Sunday. He also rushed four times for 14 yards.

injuryReports.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bucs attempted three total passes in Sunday's rain-soaked conditions, and Baker Mayfield didn't complete any of the three. Instead, Tampa Bay ran the ball 56 times and coasted to an easy win on the backs of Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell and the defense. Godwin will do battle with the Chicago secondary next Sunday, positioning the veteran wideout as a WR4 in fantasy. Emeka Egbuka (foot) could be back for that game after missing the past two contests.
injuryReports.injury: Godwin failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Bucky Irving
injuryReports.returnComment: The Buccaneers became the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a single pass, so Irving was somewhat of a one-man wrecking crew as far as the offense was concerned. The talented running back's yardage total was a career-high figure, and the performance was the third of over 100 yards for Irving already this season. The third-year back added his fifth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a four-yard run to close out the scoring with 3:47 remaining, and Irving is now up to 728 rushing yards and 5.0 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Bears next Sunday night.
injuryReports.injury: Irving rushed 27 times for 170 yards and a touchdown in the Buccaneers' 16-0 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Luke Goedeke
injuryReports.returnComment: Goedeke earned the questionable tag for Week 8 after logging a limited practice Friday, and he's been cleared by medical staff to return from a one-game absence due to a calf injury. He'll reclaim his starting spot at right tackle while Benjamin Chukwuma reverts to a depth role.
injuryReports.injury: Goedeke (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Graham Barton
injuryReports.returnComment: Barton picked up an illness over the weekend, but the third-year center has been cleared to play Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Barton (illness) is active for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Josh Hayes
injuryReports.returnComment: Hayes underwent a minor procedure on his knee after getting hurt in the preseason, and there's currently no timetable for his return following the setback. Once healthy, the 27-year-old should contribute on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Antoine Winfield Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Winfield has been sidelined for the Buccaneers' last three games while nursing a rib injury. He showed enough progression in his recovery to log a full practice Wednesday, which puts him on track to play against the Falcons on Sunday. Winfield should reclaim his starting role at safety, so Ifeatu Melifonwu figures to revert to a rotational role in the secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Winfield (ribs) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Brianna Dix of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

sources.returnComment: Cook gave the Bills some breathing room with a five-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to extend Buffalo's lead to 23-10. He was evaluated for a head injury later in the game but received clearance to return and notched one more carry after that point. After being held to 57 rushing yards without a touchdown by the Texans in Week 1, Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in six consecutive games. Extending that streak won't be easy in Week 9 against Minnesota's elite defense on MNF.

00-0034857.injury: Allen completed 21 of 34 passes for 289 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He added 30 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown on seven rushing attempts.

sources.name: Josh Allen
sources.returnComment: Allen capped the opening drive with a one-yard touchdown plunge on which he went airborne to stretch the ball over the goal line. He struggled as a passer in the first half, including a first-quarter interception, but Allen heated up after halftime to post his highest passing yards total since a 334-yard Week 1 performance. Allen's 11-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore (knee) in the fourth quarter gave Allen sole possession of first place in Bills history with 259 passing touchdowns, including postseason play. He added a 23-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Kincaid on the next drive as the Bills pulled away from a Ravens team that lost top two QBs Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe). Allen has led the Bills to a 6-1 record heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the 6-1 Vikings.

sources.returnComment: Williams helped set the tone for the Bears' statement road victory by leading a 17-play, 80-yard march that absorbed 8:32 of the first quarter, one that the third-year signal-caller capped off with a one-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden. Williams then managed the game effectively from that point forward, avoiding mistakes while leaning on a workhorse performance from D'Andre Swift (27 carries, three touchdowns) and an often dominating effort from his defense. Williams now has a three-game streak of interception-free performances and is up to 1,267 passing yards through five contests heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

workloadContext.methodology: Conditional expected-lineup research allocation, not a validated improvement to the forest. No arbitrary play probability for questionable returns. Historical coappearance is descriptive, not proof of causal injury effects. Missing player rows are not zero-filled as game outcomes.
workloadContext.scope: Current-team QB/RB/WR/TE opportunities. Archived actual statistics and sportsbook quotes are never rewritten.

tdReport.orderMethodology: First and last TD fair odds come from separate player-game models trained on actual first/last scorer IDs, including defensive/return TDs in the event order and overtime. They use lagged opportunity and prior scoring-order rates; ATTD probabilities are not reused as first/last estimates. Game-level probability caps reserve mass for unmodeled scorers and no-TD outcomes. Book settlement rules may differ.
